title: Leadpages Review 2026: Rebuilt Platform, Real Costs, Who It Fits
desc: Leadpages review 2026 after the rebuild: what Grow $99, Optimize $199 and Scale $399 include, unlimited traffic, the single login limit, who should buy.
keywords: leadpages review, leadpages review 2026, is leadpages worth it, leadpages pros and cons, leadpages landing page builder review, leadpages alternatives
body:
Quick answer: This Leadpages review covers the platform as it is in 2026, a rebuilt conversion platform rather than the page builder most people remember. At $99 a month the Grow plan gives you unlimited pages and traffic, manual A/B testing, dynamic text replacement and lead enrichment, which is a strong bundle for anyone sending paid traffic to landing pages. Its weak points are just as concrete: a one login entry tier, only 5 active integrations, AI credits that meter the editor, and a trial that needs a card and charges on day 7. This review is based on the pricing and product pages as published on September 5, 2026, and on what we see when clients bring us landing pages to fix.

What changed: the rebuild

Leadpages' own FAQ answers "How is this different from the Leadpages I know?" with a direct statement: the product was rebuilt from the ground up by the same team, with new technology. The practical result is a split into HTML Pub, a $10 to $49 publishing product, and Leadpages, a $99 to $399 conversion product (every line item is in our Leadpages pricing guide), with AI page creation, unlimited traffic and an MCP server on every Leadpages plan. Existing customers keep their price and, per the FAQ, gain A/B testing, dynamic text replacement and AI page creation at no extra charge. That is an unusually customer friendly migration and it is the first thing to say in Leadpages' favour.

What you get, plan by plan

  • Publishing: AI page creation from a prompt or a URL import, batch page creation, brand kits (3, 5 or 10), websites and blogs, custom domains with free SSL (4, 6 or 10), and 15 to 50 GB of asset storage.
  • Optimization: manual A/B testing from Grow, dynamic text replacement to match ad copy, manual personalization, then on Optimize and above Smart Traffic, click and scroll heatmaps, auto personalization, an insights dashboard and performance alerts, and on Scale a full auto optimization loop that keeps testing without intervention.
  • Lead intelligence: IP enrichment on 2,000 to 10,000 visitors a month and lead enrichment on 1,000 to 5,000 leads, ICP audience targeting and an offline conversion pixel. Leadpages positions this as knowing who is visiting before they fill a form.
  • Plumbing: forms, webhooks, CSV export, form submission history kept while subscribed, an MCP server for AI tools, and 5, 10 or 25 active integrations across HubSpot, Salesforce, Mailchimp, Google Ads, Stripe, Shopify, Slack, Zapier and, via Paragon, a claimed 200 plus more.

See the full Leadpages feature table

What we like

  • No traffic meter, on any plan. Leadpages does not cap visitors and says it charges no overages. For a paid media team whose winning campaign suddenly triples traffic, that removes the nastiest surprise a page builder can produce.
  • Testing at the entry tier. Manual A/B testing on the $99 plan, with dynamic text replacement alongside it, is the pairing that makes a landing page tool earn its keep on paid search.
  • Enrichment is built in. Identifying visiting companies and enriching leads is normally a separate subscription. It is in the base plan here, with stated monthly quotas rather than vague promises.
  • A clean upgrade path. Start on HTML Pub at $29, keep the pages and domains, move to Grow when you need testing. Nothing to rebuild.
  • Honest trial mechanics, if strict. Full access to the plan you choose, no feature restrictions, pages saved if you let the trial lapse.

What will annoy you

  • Grow is a single login. Team seats start at Optimize with 3. A two person marketing team that wants separate logins is a $199 a month customer, not a $99 one.
  • Five integrations fill up fast. Integrations are counted as active connections. CRM, email, ads, payments and chat is five, and then you are paying for Optimize's 10.
  • AI credits meter the editor. 40,000 credits a month on Grow power AI page creation, URL imports and AI chat. Heavy users will buy top ups from $2.50. It is not a hidden cost, but it is a cost the old product did not have.
  • The card required trial. Seven days, card at checkout, charged on day 7. Kit, by contrast, runs a 14 day trial with no card. Set a reminder.
  • Two variants per test on Grow. Four variants, Smart Traffic and heatmaps all live at $199 and above. If you are buying Leadpages specifically for optimization tooling, Optimize is the real entry price.
  • No native CRM, email or checkout. Leadpages is a page and conversion layer. It integrates with the rest of your stack rather than replacing it, which is fine if you have a stack and a gap if you do not.

How it compares

Against ClickFunnels, which starts at $97 a month with email marketing, courses, a store and a CRM pipeline built in, Leadpages is the narrower, deeper tool: better testing and enrichment, no all in one. We cover the trade offs in Leadpages vs ClickFunnels. Against GoHighLevel, which is a full agency CRM with funnels, calendars and automation from $97, Leadpages wins on landing page optimization and loses on everything else; if you are an agency, read our GoHighLevel vs ClickFunnels piece first, because that is usually the more relevant decision. Against Unbounce and Instapage, Leadpages' own page claims traffic caps on their $99 plans; we did not verify those rivals for this review.

Verdict: who should buy it

  • Buy Grow at $99 if you are a solo marketer or small business running paid traffic to landing pages and you want testing, dynamic text and enrichment without a second subscription.
  • Buy Optimize at $199 if you have a team, more than five integrations, or you want Smart Traffic and heatmaps to do the optimization for you.
  • Buy HTML Pub at $29 if you only need to publish pages fast with a custom domain and are not testing yet.
  • Do not buy it as an all in one. If you need email, CRM, calendars and checkout in the same login, ClickFunnels or GoHighLevel is the right shape, and our GoHighLevel developers build that stack for agencies, including the white label SaaS version agencies resell.

The landing page is the last step of the funnel. If the problem is that nobody arrives at it, our lead generation team fixes the front of the pipeline, and Leadpages is a good place to send that traffic.

What to test in the seven days

  • Dynamic text replacement on a live ad group. Point one paid search ad group at a Grow page with the headline mapped to the keyword, and compare conversion rate with the static page it replaces. This is the feature that justifies the $99.
  • Enrichment accuracy. Send a week of traffic and check how many of the 2,000 IP identifications and 1,000 lead enrichments resolve to real companies you would want to call. Quotas are only worth what they resolve.
  • The integration cap. Connect everything you actually use. If you hit five on Grow, you have learned your real price is $199 before you have paid anything.
  • AI credit burn. Build your pages with the AI editor and watch the credit counter. 40,000 a month is plenty for a few pages and thin for a batch of fifty.
  • Set the day six reminder. The card is charged on day 7. Decide on day six.

Fit by business type

A local service business running Google Ads to two or three offers fits Grow exactly: one login, a handful of integrations, testing and dynamic text, and the enrichment quota is more than the traffic will use. A SaaS marketing team fits Optimize, where seats, Smart Traffic and heatmaps earn their keep on higher traffic pages. An agency fits Scale or does not fit at all, depending on whether it wants workspaces and audit logs inside Leadpages or a client CRM with pages attached. A creator selling a course fits HTML Pub Pro at $29 until launch day, then Grow. A B2B company whose real problem is pipeline volume does not fit any landing page tool until the top of the funnel is solved.

faqs: For marketers sending paid traffic to landing pages, yes: the $99 Grow plan includes unlimited pages and traffic, manual A/B testing, dynamic text replacement and lead enrichment, a bundle that usually costs two or three subscriptions elsewhere. It is not worth it as an all in one, because it has no native CRM, email marketing or checkout.
What are the downsides of Leadpages?

The $99 plan is a single login with no team seats, integrations are capped at 5 active connections, AI credits meter the editor with top ups from $2.50, the trial requires a card and charges on day 7, and A/B tests on Grow allow only 2 variants. Smart Traffic and heatmaps start at $199.
Does Leadpages include A/B testing and heatmaps?

Manual A/B testing is included from the $99 Grow plan with 2 variants per test. Click and scroll heatmaps, Smart Traffic and auto personalization start on the $199 Optimize plan, and the fully automated optimization loop is on the $399 Scale plan. HTML Pub plans do not include testing.

No. Every Leadpages plan lists unlimited traffic and the FAQ states there are no overage fees or penalties when campaigns succeed. Page counts are also unlimited on Leadpages plans; the cheaper HTML Pub plans cap pages at 5, 25 and 50.

Leadpages if you want the better landing page optimization tooling and already have email and CRM elsewhere. ClickFunnels if you want funnels, email marketing, courses, a store and a CRM pipeline in one subscription from $97 a month. Agencies usually need the second shape, and GoHighLevel is a third option built specifically for them.
How does the Leadpages free trial work?

Seven days with full access to whichever plan you choose. A credit card is collected at checkout and charged on day 7 unless you cancel from account settings before then, which Leadpages says carries no charge. If you do not pick a plan, the account pauses and your pages stay saved.
